statement: In Gemma 4 E2B (google/gemma-4-E2B-it rev 3e22461, transformers 5.20.2), large sampled perturbations (Gaussian, sd 50) of the residual stream at all non-final positions entering layers 15, 16, 25 or 34 left final-position logits exactly unchanged, while the same perturbations entering layers 5, 13 or 14 changed them (max |Δlogit| 17.7-36.4). Together with the implementation (layers >= 15 read only K/V stored by layers 13/14), this indicates non-final positions after layer 14 are causally inert for final-position outputs.
scope: Gemma 4 E2B text decoder, inputs shorter than the 512-token sliding window, no KV cache, fp32 compute; implementation in transformers 5.20.2

supporting_evidence.summary: Gaussian noise (sd 50) on all non-final positions: max|Δlogit| = 0.0 at layers 15/16/25/34 vs 17.7-36.4 at layers 5/13/14; 2 prompts; identical in two separate runs
code: layers >= num_layers - num_kv_shared_layers (=15) take K/V from shared_kv_states stored by the last non-shared layer of the same type (13 sliding, 14 full)

conditions: 2 prompts (10 and 15 tokens); noise sd 50 per coordinate; Runner hooks at resid_pre
verification_method: Deterministic perturbation test + source-code reading; preregistered as P-ARCH-1 in experiments/E001_arch/PREREG.md
uncertainty: Behaviour with KV cache / generation and inputs longer than the sliding window not tested; a different implementation (e.g. official JAX) could differ only if it diverges from the HF reference.

statement: Under the logit lens (final RMSNorm → tied unembedding → softcap 30) applied to the final-position residual stream of Gemma 4 E2B-IT, the correct single-token answer to 60 correctly answered factual prompts first becomes top-1 at residual index 26-34 (median 28, bootstrap 95% CI [28, 29]); it stays top-1 at all subsequent layers (median fraction 1.0), and its median rank at indices 0-5 is ~1.1e5 of 262 144.
scope: google/gemma-4-E2B-it; 62 English factual prompts (32 landmark→city, 30 country→capital; 60 answered correctly); residual index k = input to layer k (35 = final residual); logit lens only (no tuned lens)

statement: In Gemma 4 E2B-IT factual recall on short prompts, the subject information that determines the answer reaches the final position through the K/V stored by layer 13 (read by KV-shared layers 15-34), not through the K/V stored by layer 14: replacing the corrupt run's layer-13 stored K/V by the clean one recovers a median 0.986 of the logit difference (relation-stratified subject-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [0.923, 1.014]) vs 0.017 [0.009, 0.027] for layer 14 (28 held-out pairs); the effect is carried by the subject-span positions (0.980) and not by template positions (0.006). The same pattern holds in the pretrained base checkpoint google/gemma-4-E2B on a disjoint set of 28 held-out pairs (KV13_all 0.994 [cluster CI 0.949, 1.022] vs KV14_all -0.001 [-0.040, 0.018]), i.e. it is not a product of instruction tuning.
scope: google/gemma-4-E2B-it and google/gemma-4-E2B (base); two relations (landmark->city 12 pairs, country->capital 16 pairs) with single-token answers; prompts 7-14 tokens (far below the 512-token sliding window, so this distinguishes the two stored K/V tensors, not sliding vs full attention); counterfactual patching with logit-difference recovery

supporting_evidence.summary: preregistered P1-P3 pass on held-out pairs; NULL control max|r| 1.1e-6; R2-only (never used before) KV13_all 0.982 vs KV14_all 0.017
consistent precursor: last-subject resid patch recovery 0.595 at layer 13 vs 0.010 at layer 14

statement: In the tested factual-recall assay on Gemma 4 E2B-IT, block-25 attention at the final position is the largest single-layer causal contributor among the 20 KV-shared layers: patching only its clean attention contribution into the corrupt run recovers a median 0.757 (relation-stratified subject-cluster CI [0.625, 0.826]; largest of 20 single-layer patches in 28/28 held-out pairs), and substituting the corrupt run's contribution leaves a median 0.227 at block 25 vs per-layer medians >= 0.929 at every other KV-shared layer (individual pairs down to 0.85 at layer 31). Head 0 of block 25 had the strongest individual effect (single-head corruption leaves 0.37 vs >= 0.98 for heads 1-7; multi-head interactions untested) and puts a median 0.88 of its final-query attention on the positions where the two prompts differ. Block 25 is not necessary: replacing its contribution by a leave-one-out mean retains 0.80 [cluster CI 0.75, 0.89], by a norm-matched mean 0.78, and zeroing it retains 0.94 (E006c) - wrong-subject content is harmful, absent content is not. Head 0 is the only head that matters under corruption (heads 1-7 jointly corrupted retain 0.96) and attends with median mass 0.87 to the verified subject token span. Mean-ablating the final-position attention of all 20 KV-shared layers gives 0.46 [0.34, 0.52], the same as mean-ablating attention in all 35 layers (0.46 [0.34, 0.52], the subject-agnostic neutral point of this metric), while ablating final-position attention in layers 0-14 leaves 1.01: all subject information that reaches the answer position arrives through KV-shared attention. Relative to that neutral point, block-25 mean ablation leaves about 63% of the subject preference, i.e. other KV-shared layers carry it redundantly, but no single one is critical (min joint ablation 0.74). In the base checkpoint the same layer (block 25, largest in 28/28 pairs; sufficiency 0.654) and the same head (head 0: 0.423; other heads <= 0.06) dominate; corruption of block 25 leaves more of the logit difference in base (0.337 [0.268, 0.453]) than in IT (0.227).
scope: as K-0006 (two relations, short prompts, IT checkpoint); head-level results from E006b (preregistered Q1, Q4 exploratory)

statement: In the HF transformers 5.20.2 implementation (all 35 decoder layers run at every prompt position), computing Gemma 4 E2B-IT layers 15-34 only at the final position during a single-sequence forward leaves the final-position logits numerically equivalent (max |diff| <= 3.1e-5; same top-1 and same top-10 set) for T = 64-1024 tokens, including T = 1024 beyond the 512-token sliding window, and reduces wall time by a median 1.8x (T=64), 2.4x (256), 2.7x (512) and 3.3x (1024; 2.6x by min/min) over 3 interleaved repeats on a shared 2-vCPU host with fp32 compute. Exploratory (post hoc): at T = 2048 the full computation exceeded a 6.8 GB RSS guard (logs/memwatch.log 10:32:57Z, process_metrics rc=3) while the reduced one completed (58 s).
scope: single sequence, batch 1, CPU (AVX-512F, no bf16 GEMM), fp32 compute with bf16 weights, final-position output only (first generated token); decode with KV cache, batching and GPU not measured; energy not measurable in this sandbox

supporting_evidence.summary: preregistered P1 exactness, P2 >=2x for T>=256, P4 trend pass; T=2048 FULL missing (RSS guard)
exploratory: SKIP at T=2048 completes; FULL vs SKIP peak RSS growth at T=1024 0.35 vs 0.12 GB (allocator-order confounded)
K-0001/K-0002: non-final positions inert after layer 14

YOCO (Sun et al. 2024, arXiv 2405.05254) states the principle for decoder-decoder models: 'the computation flow enables prefilling to early exit without changing the final output' (quote checked in papers/txt/2405.05254.txt)

statement: A DoLa-style layer contrast (final log-prob minus log-prob at the max-JSD premature residual in 26-30, plausibility filter 0.1) does not significantly improve Gemma 4 E2B-IT first-token factual accuracy: TEST 42.7% vs 41.4% greedy (12 items fixed, 7 broken, exact McNemar p = 0.36, n = 396). In the base checkpoint google/gemma-4-E2B the same procedure lowers accuracy (TEST 44.7% vs 48.0% greedy; 15 fixed, 28 broken, exact McNemar p = 0.066; 7% of items broken, above the preregistered 3% harm bound).
scope: google/gemma-4-E2B-it and google/gemma-4-E2B (base); factset_v1 (793 single-word completions over 20 relations, generated and cross-verified by two API model families); raw completion prompts with BOS; first-token correctness (mixes knowledge with answer form, see E009 exploratory); bucket chosen on DEV half

statement: In Gemma 4 E2B-IT the logit lens at the final position reaches answer-level first-token accuracy only late (factset DEV accuracy by residual index: <= 1% up to index 25, 10.6% at 27, 36.3% at 29, peak 47.6% at 33, 37.5% at the output). Consequently a confidence-threshold early exit (first index >= 20 whose lens max-prob >= tau, tau chosen on DEV) skips only 4.9% of decoder layers on TEST; it does not cost accuracy (47.2% vs 41.4%) because the last block lowers first-token accuracy on this metric. The base checkpoint shows the same pattern: best lens index 33 on DEV, TEST accuracy at index 33 exceeds the output by 3.3 points (IT 6.1), 148 errors with the target top-1 at some index 20-34 (IT 151), and early exit at the DEV-chosen threshold skips 0.5% of layers.
scope: google/gemma-4-E2B-it and google/gemma-4-E2B (base); factset_v1 raw completions; first-token correctness (answer-form effects such as ' **' or first names count as errors); logit lens = final norm + tied unembedding + softcap

supporting_evidence.summary: preregistered P-c1 fails: 4.9% of layers skipped (< 15% predicted)
post hoc: accuracy by residual index; 151/480 errors had the target top-1 at some index 20-34
early-exit potential diminishes in newer model generations and smaller models (consistent direction)
K-0005: answer emergence median index 28 on 60 easy prompts (consistent)
base: lost answers 148, markdown top-1 errors 0, idx33 - final +3.3 pp

uncertainty: The late-layer accuracy drop is post hoc; the base test (H-017) showed it is not an instruction-tuning artefact (only the markdown variant is IT-specific); it may partly reflect logit-lens miscalibration at index 33. Lens (not tuned lens) underestimates early decodability.
